definition: A machine learning paradigm where an agent learns to take actions in an environment to maximize cumulative reward through trial and error.
details: Reinforcement learning combines ideas from optimal control and behavioral psychology, and is used both in classic sequential decision-making problems (like game playing) and, more recently, as part of aligning LLMs via human feedback.
story: Imagine a video game where the only feedback is the score ticking up or down — and you learn by playing a million rounds. Think of it this way: A machine learning paradigm where an agent learns to take actions in an environment to maximize cumulative reward through trial and error. And here is the clever part: Reinforcement learning combines ideas from optimal control and behavioral psychology, and is used both in classic sequential decision-making problems (like game playing) and, more recently, as part of aligning LLMs via human feedback. Reward, not instructions, is the teacher. And that is Reinforcement Learning — skill forged from consequences.
